examples.text: We saw a breakdown by the side of the road.

examples.text: After so much stress, he suffered a breakdown and simply gave up.

examples.text: England beat Georgia in their Pool B World Cup match in Dunedin but the stuttering nature of the performance will be of concern to manager Martin Johnson. glosses: An act of splitting logs of wood using a large saw in a sawmill; also, the saw used; or (rare) the building in which the process is carried out.

examples.text: And now it's time for a breakdown.

glosses: Synonym of percussion break (“a percussion-focused segment of a song, chosen by a hip-hop DJ to manipulate through cutting, mixing, and other techniques in order to create rhythmic music”).
A section of a song, typical in hardcore music and related styles (such as metalcore, grindcore, and deathcore), characterized by a lower tempo and greater heaviness and intensity of sound.

examples.text: The fired-up foursome [Trial] takes itself very seriously, singing politically charged lyrics, which, in the tradition of Strife and Damnation AD, are strategically placed in the middle of slamming, moshable breakdowns.

glosses: A noisy, rapid, shuffling dance engaged in competitively by a number of individuals or pairs in succession, common among African-Americans from the Southern United States; also, a lively event, chiefly in a rural setting, at which such dancing is done; a hoedown, a shindig.

examples.text: Come, hold on, boys, do n't clear out when the quadrilles are over, for we are going to have a break down to wind up with.

A fiddle, a banjo, and a clarinet—these were the instruments. The trio took their places side by side, and began to play some rattling dance-music, and beat time with their big boots.

glosses: A piece of music played for such a dance, especially a rapid bluegrass tune featuring a five-string banjo.

examples.text: Without a change of countenance, as if he were deaf to her entreaties and threats, he tuned up the banjo, and played a breakdown.

Mama loves you. I left you a good pair of shoes in there on the kitchen table. They shine up easy."

glosses: A part of something that has been divided.

examples.text: Monarchies where partition isn't prohibited risk weakening through parcellation and civil wars between the heirs.

glosses: A vertical structure that divides a room.

examples.text: a brick partition; lath and plaster partitions

glosses: That which divides or separates; that by which different things, or distinct parts of the same thing, are separated; boundary; dividing line or space.

examples.text: No sight could pass / Betwixt the nice partitions of the grass.

glosses: A part divided off by walls; an apartment; a compartment.

examples.text: Lodged in a small partition.

glosses: The severance of common or undivided interests, particularly in real estate. It may be effected by consent of parties, or by compulsion of law.

examples.text: The epicenter of the disturbance is the partition currently housing a [personality construct array] retrieved from Contender AI 05-032 <+> 0816.

glosses: A division of a database or one of its constituting elements such as tables into separate independent parts.

A collection of non-empty, disjoint subsets of a set whose union is the set itself (i.e. all elements of the set are contained in exactly one of the subsets).
A musical score.

examples.text: to partition a hard drive

glosses: To divide a region or country into two or more territories with separate political status.

examples.text: Poland was progressively partitioned by Russia, Austria, and Prussia in the late 18th century.
